key_insight: A proposed photonic Maxwell’s demon uses wavelength-selective mirrors and irreversible wavelength conversion to admit sunlight while trapping converted radiation for energy use.
engineering_relevance: The concept could improve solar-thermal storage and thermophotovoltaic conversion through repeated photon recycling and nearly complete optical utilization in the ideal limit.
method: Pair a multilayer dielectric mirror with a material that irreversibly converts transmitted photons to longer wavelengths.
Construct a 3D enclosure that admits visible light and reflects converted infrared radiation inward.
Combine the enclosure with a blackbody absorber and, for thermophotovoltaics, an ultra-low-bandgap photovoltaic cell.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a theoretical proposal and analysis, citing the 93.3% Landsberg limit as an ideal thermodynamic target rather than a demonstrated efficiency.
watch_item: Real performance depends on nonideal spectral selectivity, conversion losses, and heat leakage; no experimental validation or AI method is reported in the abstract.
paper_title: Photonic Maxwells demon as an energy resource
